title: Pattern-anodyne generators, fibered lifting and external products
statement:
Use the small fully scaled categorical patterns $\mathfrak P=(C,S,\{p_\alpha:K_\alpha^{\triangleleft}\to C\})$ and their fibered marked objects from [def-coef-categorical-pattern-fibrancy], and marked simplicial sets, $(-)^\flat$, $(-)^\sharp$, coordinatewise product markings and marked internal Homs from [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model]. Use standard simplices, boundaries, horns and Kan fibrations from [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. A weakly saturated closure means closure under pushouts, small transfinite compositions and retracts, including isomorphisms. Right lifting against a map means existence of a diagonal in every commuting square. Let $J_{\mathfrak P}$ be the following small set of maps of marked simplicial sets over $\bar C=(C,S)$, with every possible indicated base map:

(A0) $(\Lambda^2_1)^\sharp\amalg_{(\Lambda^2_1)^\flat}(\Delta^2)^\flat\to(\Delta^2)^\sharp$, over triangles all of whose edges lie in $S$.

(A1) $Q^\flat\to Q^\sharp$, over maps carrying every edge of $Q$ into $S$, where $Q=\Delta^0\amalg_{\Delta^{\{0,2\}}}\Delta^3\amalg_{\Delta^{\{1,3\}}}\Delta^0$ collapses the indicated edges.

(B0) $\{0\}^\sharp\to(\Delta^1)^\sharp$, over an edge of $S$.

(B1) $K_\alpha^\sharp\to(K_\alpha^{\triangleleft})^\sharp$, over $p_\alpha$.

(C0) $(\Lambda^n_0,\{01\})\to(\Delta^n,\{01\})$ for $n>1$, over any simplex of $C$ whose edge $01$ lies in $S$. Here $(U,\{01\})$ marks that edge and all degenerate edges, and no others.

(C1) $(\Lambda^n_i)^\flat\to(\Delta^n)^\flat$ for $0<i<n$, over any simplex of $C$.

(C2) For $n\geq1$, $\alpha$, and any map $\Delta^n\star K_\alpha\to C$ restricting to $p_\alpha$ on $\{n\}\star K_\alpha$, the inclusion
$$
(\partial\Delta^n\star K_\alpha)^\flat\amalg_{(\{n\}\star K_\alpha)^\flat}(\{n\}\star K_\alpha)^\sharp
\longrightarrow
(\Delta^n\star K_\alpha)^\flat\amalg_{(\{n\}\star K_\alpha)^\flat}(\{n\}\star K_\alpha)^\sharp.
$$
The simplicial join $U\star V$ has $n$-simplices $\coprod_{i+j=n-1,\ i,j\geq-1}U_i\times V_j$, with $U_{-1}=V_{-1}=\{*\}$ and the face and degeneracy maps given by their positions in the ordered concatenation. Empty $K_\alpha$ are allowed. Every $2$-simplex is scaled, so no additional triangle restriction is required in (A0), (A1), or (C0).

Call the weakly saturated closure of $J_{\mathfrak P}$ the $\mathfrak P$-anodyne maps. All these maps are injective on underlying simplices. A marked object over $\bar C$ is $\mathfrak P$-fibered if and only if its terminal map has the right lifting property against $J_{\mathfrak P}$.

Let $\mathfrak P_0$ be the pattern on $\Delta^0$ with all edges marked and with no cones. Its fibered objects are precisely $D^\natural$, for quasicategories $D$ with exactly their equivalence edges marked. For a degreewise injective map $i:A\to A'$ over $\bar C$ and a degreewise injective marked map $j:L\to L'$, form
$$i\mathbin\square j:(A'\times L)\amalg_{A\times L}(A\times L')\to A'\times L'.$$
If $i$ is $\mathfrak P$-anodyne or $j$ is $\mathfrak P_0$-anodyne, then $i\mathbin\square j$ is $\mathfrak P$-anodyne.

For any $\mathfrak P$-fibered $Z$ and any $A\to\bar C$, the simplicial set $\operatorname{Map}^\sharp_C(A,Z)_n=\operatorname{Hom}_{/\bar C}(A\times(\Delta^n)^\sharp,Z)$ is Kan. Restriction along any degreewise injective $i:A\to A'$ is a Kan fibration on these simplicial sets, and is a trivial Kan fibration when $i$ is $\mathfrak P$-anodyne. These assertions concern the explicit maps and lifting properties, without assuming a model structure on the pattern slice.

source.place: Higher Algebra, Definition B.1.1, Proposition B.1.6, Proposition B.1.9 specialized to a second pattern trivial on a point, and Proposition B.1.14, printed pp.1470-1482. For triviality of restriction along a P-anodyne map, use the proof of B.1.14 together with B.1.9, as in Example B.2.2. The point-pattern identification is Example B.0.21 and the definition of cocartesian edges over a point. Read online 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result. The printed final sentence of B.1.14 says P0-anodyne although f is over P; its proof and Example B.2.2 give the P-anodyne assertion used here.
